key_insight: WorldDirector separates motion planning from image generation, letting a model control objects and camera paths independently. This enables persistent dynamic memory and freer viewpoint changes in video world simulation.
problem_solved: Existing world models often mix physical dynamics with rendering and depend on continuous visual input to keep motion going. This makes them hard to control, weak at long-term object persistence, and limited in exploring new viewpoints.
method: Use an LLM to orchestrate semantic motion, including 3D object trajectories and camera movements.
Decouple motion control from visual synthesis so dynamics can persist without constant frame-by-frame visual conditioning.
Generate videos/world simulations from the planned motions while supporting unrestricted viewpoint exploration.
impact: This makes world models more controllable, modular, and useful for interactive simulation, robotics, and content generation. Practitioners gain a way to design scenes with persistent objects and editable camera behavior.

paper_title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
paper_authors: Hanlin Wang, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Wen Wang, Qingyan Bai
